subject: Clarify billing path & co-sell credit timing for Brightleaf procurement
messages:
From: Marta Kowalski <marta.k@brightleaf.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@brightleaf.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Procurement question: marketplace vs MSA (billing & co-sell credits)

Hi Hannah,

We're preparing the purchase paperwork for Brightleaf's pilot and need a quick decision on purchase path. Finance is leaning toward buying through AWS Marketplace (private offer) because it keeps our invoicing on a single vendor and speeds PO approval. Legal prefers signing Redwood's MSA / SOW directly because of indemnity and data residency clauses.

Two quick operational questions we need answered for procurement sign-off:
1) If we accept a Private Offer on AWS, who is shown as the invoice sponsor and seller of record? Will the invoice come from Redwood or from an AWS-sponsored reseller?
2) How/when do co-sell credits get assigned to Redwood if we go via Marketplace private offer vs direct invoice under an MSA? Is there any lag that affects Redwood's ability to recognize revenue or our partner credits?

We've attached our procurement questionnaire — the finance team would like an example invoice and a brief checklist of tradeoffs so they can finish PO routing. We're on a tight timetable (end of quarter).

Thanks,
Marta
Procurement Lead, Brightleaf Analytics
Attachment: brightleaf_procurement_questions.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Kowalski <marta.k@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Procurement question: marketplace vs MSA (billing & co-sell credits)

Marta — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. High-level answers up front, then a recommended path based on what you described.

Short answers:
- Invoice / seller of record: With an AWS Private Offer configured as "Redwood as seller of record," the invoice will come from Redwood (aws will only facilitate payment routing). If you accept a sponsored offer (seller is a reseller/SaaS partner), the invoice will show the sponsor as the seller. We can ensure Redwood is the merchant_of_record for your private offer; that's our default for enterprise deals.
- Co-sell credits timing: Co-sell credit assignment depends on the marketplace flow. For AWS private offers where Redwood is seller_of_record and the transaction is registered, co-sell credits typically register within AWS reporting cycles — expect a 30–60 day delay in visible crediting in partner reports. For direct MSA invoicing (Redwood issues the invoice), revenue recognition and partner crediting are immediate to us (no marketplace lag).

Tradeoffs & recommendation:
- Marketplace private offer (Redwood as seller_of_record): fast PO processing on your side, standard net30/60 terms via AWS billing manager, less procurement friction. Downside: slight delay in partner credit reporting and occasionally extra metadata requirements for SKU mapping.
- Direct MSA / Redwood invoice: gives you more flexible contract terms (termination, indemnity, SLAs) and gives Redwood immediate revenue recognition. Procurement may push back due to multiple vendors on their ledger.

Recommended path for Brightleaf: If legal requires MSA-level protections, we can sign the MSA and still do an AWS private offer for payment (MSA governs terms, private offer used solely for PO/invoice flow). That hybrid preserves legal protections and keeps your finance happy with single-vendor procurement.

Next steps I can own:
- Share a sample AWS-sponsored invoice that shows Redwood as seller (attached).
- Draft a 1-page mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for contracting, PO, and pilot start.
- Confirm whether Brightleaf requires PO number on the invoice and whether your AP team needs supplier tax id / EU VAT notes.

I'll loop Soojin on the SKU/integration and Jordan on pricing adjustments for private-offer SKUs. Can you confirm your AP contact and desired payment terms (Net30/Net45/Prepay)?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sample_aws_sponsored_invoice_redwood.pdf (pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Kowalski <marta.k@brightleaf.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Procurement question: marketplace vs MSA (billing & co-sell credits)

Hi Marta — quick technical addendum from Sales Engineering / GTM: 

1) SKU mapping & attribution: If you take a private offer, we'll map the Brightleaf commitment to the private-offer SKU (this ensures usage and seats reconcile in AWS billing). That mapping is important so co-sell registration picks up the deal correctly.
2) Co-sell credit flow: Practically, co-sell credits are only visible in AWS Partner reports after the marketplace settlement cycle completes. That means Redwood's partner portal will show the credit 4–8 weeks after invoice settlement in many cases (your finance timelines unaffected, but our internal partner crediting lags reporting).
3) Edge cases: If finance requires a remit-to that is a reseller, we can still structure a private offer but must flag that seller_of_record differs — that will change tax/VAT lines on the invoice and can complicate your AP reconciliation.

Recommended: Hybrid path (MSA + private offer with Redwood as merchant_of_record). We'll prepare:
- A short MAP with dates and who signs which doc.
- A sample invoice that includes PO and EU VAT note.

If useful, I can join your procurement call this week to walk AP through the invoice fields.

— Soojin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Our legal team is happy with the hybrid approach (MSA + private offer) as long as Redwood will be merchant_of_record and the MSA is referenced on the invoice. That would satisfy both teams.

We need to get the PO in place by Friday to hit our internal quarter close. If you can share the sample invoice and a one-page MAP, we can route today.

Regards,
